title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 8 (Formation of Companies with Charitable Objects)

content.overview: Section 8 provides for formation of companies with charitable or other useful objects where profits are applied to promoting those objects and no dividend is paid to members. Such companies obtain a licence from the Central Government and enjoy specified privileges and restrictions.
content.glance: State the charitable/useful objects requirement; note the no-dividend rule; explain the Central Government licence and the privileges/restrictions of a s. 8 company.
content.study: Section 8 companies are formed for the promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any other useful object. The profits, if any, are applied solely to promoting the objects, and no dividend is distributed to members. The Central Government may grant a licence for registration as a limited company without the addition of the word ‘Limited’ or ‘Private Limited’ to its name. Section 8 companies are subject to conditions in the licence and to restrictions on alteration of objects and on transfer of membership in certain cases. Revocation of licence and conversion pathways are also regulated. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 8 and distinguish ordinary limited companies under ss. 3–7.

sections.heading: Qualifying Objects
sections.body: Promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, environment or other useful object.

sections.heading: Application of Profits
sections.body: Profits must be applied solely to promoting the objects; no dividend to members.

sections.heading: Licence and Name
sections.body: Central Government licence; company may omit ‘Limited’ / ‘Private Limited’ from its name.

sections.heading: Restrictions and Revocation
sections.body: Licence conditions; restrictions on object alteration and certain transfers; power to revoke licence.

provisions.title: Formation of companies with charitable objects, etc.

examples.title: Educational trust company
examples.body: A company is formed solely for educational objects with profits applied to education and no dividend. Section 8 licence route applies.

examples.title: Dividend declared by s. 8 company
examples.body: A s. 8 company declares a dividend to members. This breaches the statutory condition and may attract licence revocation and other consequences.

hypotheticals.question: Can a s. 8 company distribute profits to members?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 8 requires that profits be applied solely to promoting the objects; dividend distribution is prohibited.

hypotheticals.question: Must a s. 8 company use the word ‘Limited’?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. With a Central Government licence it may omit ‘Limited’ or ‘Private Limited’ from its name.

distinctions.title: Section 8 company vs ordinary limited company
distinctions.left: Charitable/useful objects; no dividend; licence; name privilege
distinctions.right: Commercial objects; dividend permitted; standard ‘Limited’ name

misconceptions.trap: Any non-profit entity is automatically a s. 8 company.
misconceptions.correction: Section 8 requires formation under the Companies Act with a Central Government licence and compliance with statutory conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Section 8 companies may freely pay dividends.
misconceptions.correction: Dividend to members is prohibited; profits must promote the objects.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.
cases.relevance: Already in file; s. 8 companies also obtain separate personality on registration.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 8 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify objects. II. Check profit-application and no-dividend rule. III. Note licence and name. IV. State restrictions. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Objects analysis; profit application; licence status; name privilege; restrictions; precise relief.

examTips: Mention the licence and name privilege.
